info.name: MCP Auth Policy - Manual Test
info.description:
Manual end-to-end test for the `mcp-auth`/`mcp-authz` gateway policies: the gatewayHost/gatewayUrl port-handling and precedence fixes, plus a policy-params `additionalProperties` validation check (denied vs allowed unknown params).

Prerequisites for folders 1-2 (see gateway/it/docker-compose.test.yaml):
1. `cd gateway/it`
2. `docker compose -f docker-compose.test.yaml -p gateway-it up -d gateway-controller gateway-runtime mcp-server-backend mock-jwks mock-platform-api`
3. Make sure nothing else is already bound to ports 9090 (controller) or 8080 (router).

Folder 3 needs a DIFFERENT stack (root docker-compose.yaml, real ngrok/Asgardeo) — see its own description before running it; do not run folder 3 against the plain folder-1/2 stack. Folder 4 runs on the SAME default IT stack as folders 1/2/5/6 (gatewayhost/gatewayurl are permanently configured in test-config.toml).

Run folder "1 - MCP Auth Functional Test" top to bottom to exercise the full auth flow. Run folder "2 - Policy Params Validation (additionalProperties)" to see an unknown param rejected by mcp-acl-list (additionalProperties: false) vs silently accepted by cors AND mcp-auth (additionalProperties unset/true — mcp-auth and mcp-authz were both changed from false to true) at deploy time. Run folder "3 - Real-World ngrok + Asgardeo Test" against a gateway started from the root docker-compose.yaml with an ngrok tunnel and a real Asgardeo tenant configured — see wso2-enterprise/wso2-apim-internal#19345. Run folder "4 - gatewayUrl Precedence (E2E)" (same default IT stack) to prove gatewayUrl wins over both gatewayHost and a REAL, actually-routing vhost, through the live config.toml resolution pipeline. Run folder "5 - MCP Authz Functional Test" (same default IT stack as folder 1) to exercise mcp-authz's scope-based tool authorization end-to-end. Run folder "6 - MCP Authz Policy Params Validation (additionalProperties)" (same stack) to confirm mcp-authz also now silently accepts an unknown param.

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{mcpAuthProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: MCP Auth Postman Test
  version: v1.0
  context: {{mcpAuthContext}}
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: mcp-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers:
          - mock-jwks
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: Deploys an Mcp proxy fronting mcp-server-backend, protected by mcp-auth with issuer 'mock-jwks' (already registered as a key manager in it/test-config.toml).

exec: pm.test('WWW-Authenticate points at protected-resource metadata', function () {
pm.test('authorization_servers lists the mock-jwks issuer', function () {

item.name: 1.4 Get JWT Token from Mock JWKS

request.description: mock-jwks also accepts &scope=... and &claim_<name>=<value> query params if you want to exercise requiredScopes/claim-based scenarios.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 200 with a valid token', function () {

item.name: 2 - Policy Params Validation (additionalProperties)
item.description: Confirms that whether an unknown/extra policyParam is rejected at deploy time depends entirely on the individual policy's own JSON schema setting `additionalProperties: false` — it is not enforced platform-wide, and it can change: mcp-auth and mcp-authz were BOTH switched from `false` to `true` (now silently accept unknown params, same as cors) — see 2.3. mcp-acl-list still sets `false` and is used here as the current denied-case example instead. See gateway-controller/pkg/config/policy_validator.go's validatePolicyParams (gojsonschema.Validate).

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{addPropsDeniedProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: AdditionalProperties Denied Test
  version: v1.0
  context: /addpropsdenied
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: mcp-acl-list
      version: v1
      params:
        tools:
          mode: allow
        unknownExtraParam: "should-be-rejected"
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: mcp-acl-list's policy-definition.yaml sets `additionalProperties: false` at the top level of `parameters` (mcp-auth and mcp-authz used to as well, but were both switched to `true` — see 2.3), so 'unknownExtraParam' should fail gojsonschema validation and the deploy should be rejected before it is ever persisted. No cleanup needed — nothing gets created.

exec: pm.test('Error mentions the unrecognized property', function () {

item.name: 2.2 [Allowed] cors silently accepts unknown param (additionalProperties unset)

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{addPropsAllowedProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: AdditionalProperties Allowed Test
  version: v1.0
  context: /addpropsallowed
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: cors
      version: v1
      params:
        allowedOrigins:
          - "http://example.com"
        unknownExtraParam: "silently-accepted"
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: cors's policy-definition.yaml never sets `additionalProperties` on its top-level `parameters` object, so it defaults to true (allowed) per JSON Schema semantics. 'unknownExtraParam' passes validation and the deploy succeeds despite being unrecognized by the policy.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 201 (accepted despite unknown param)', function () {

item.name: 2.3 [Allowed] mcp-auth now silently accepts unknown param (additionalProperties changed to true)

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{mcpAuthAllowedProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: MCP Auth AdditionalProperties Now Allowed Test
  version: v1.0
  context: /mcpauthallowed
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: mcp-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers:
          - mock-jwks
        unknownExtraParam: "silently-accepted"
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: mcp-auth's top-level `parameters.additionalProperties` was changed from `false` to `true` (see gateway-controllers commit 44610a1 / 7079679 on the mcp branch), so it now behaves like cors: an unrecognized param no longer blocks deploy. This test locks in that intentional behavior change so a future revert is caught.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 201 (accepted despite unknown param)', function () {

item.name: 2.5 Cleanup - Delete mcp-auth allowed test proxy
3 - Real-World ngrok + Asgardeo Test
item.description:
Validates the mcp-auth port-handling fixes against a real ngrok tunnel + real Asgardeo tenant + real (Choreo-hosted) MCP server — the exact scenario from wso2-enterprise/wso2-apim-internal#19345, where gatewayHost was set to an ngrok domain (no port) and the gateway generated a wrong protected-resource-metadata URL (localhost, then a spurious :8443) instead of the real ngrok host with no port at all.

Prerequisites:
1. Start the gateway from the root docker-compose.yaml (NOT the IT stack): `docker compose up -d gateway-controller gateway-runtime`, from a build that includes the dev-policies/mcp-auth fix.
2. `configs/config.toml` must have `policy_configurations.mcpauth_v1.gatewayhost` (lowercase!) set to your ngrok domain, and `policy_configurations.jwtauth_v1.keymanagers` pointing at your real Asgardeo tenant.
3. `ngrok http https://localhost:8443` running, with `ngrokHost` below matching its printed domain.
4. Set `realAdminPass` to the password scripts/setup.sh printed for your local gateway-controller.

Run 3.1 then 3.2 to prove the fix; run 3.3 to clean up. Connecting an actual MCP client (e.g. Claude) to `https://{{ngrokHost}}{{realMcpProxyContext}}/mcp` is the final step, done outside Postman.

item.name: 3.1 Deploy MCP Proxy (real Choreo upstream, real Asgardeo issuer)

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{realMcpProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: Order Status MCP Server
  version: v1.0
  context: {{realMcpProxyContext}}
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: {{realMcpUpstreamUrl}}
  policies:
    - name: mcp-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers:
          - PrimaryIDP
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: Deploys against the LOCAL controller (localhost:9090) — the gateway itself isn't exposed via ngrok for management, only its data-plane router (8443) is.

item.name: 3.2 Get Protected Resource Metadata via ngrok (no port, real Asgardeo issuer)

request.description: The fixes under test: (1) gatewayhost (lowercase) is actually picked up from config.toml instead of silently falling back to 'localhost'; (2) an Authority with no port (ngrok's public side is always implicit standard HTTPS/443) maps to the scheme's real standard port, not the gateway's internal 8443 — so no port is appended at all.

exec: pm.test('resource is the ngrok host with NO port', function () {
pm.test('authorization_servers points at the real Asgardeo tenant, not the gateway', function () {

item.name: 4 - gatewayUrl Precedence (E2E)
item.description:
Proves gatewayUrl's precedence over BOTH gatewayHost and vhost against a REAL config.toml resolution pipeline (config.toml -> ConfigResolver -> materialized systemParameters), not just the unit tests that construct params maps directly and can't catch a real TOML-parsing/casing mistake — see gateway-controllers commit 44610a1 and mcp_policies.feature's gatewayurl precedence scenarios.

Runs on the SAME default IT stack as folders 1/2/5/6 — test-config.toml permanently sets BOTH `policy_configurations.mcpauth_v1.gatewayhost = "mcp-e2e-gatewayhost.example.com:9443"` AND `.gatewayurl = "https://mcp-e2e-gatewayurl.example.com:7777"` at once, so no special override compose/config is needed anymore.

Run 4.1 -> 4.2 -> 4.3 to prove gatewayUrl wins over both the vhost the proxy is deployed with AND the gatewayHost also configured for mcp-auth's own 401. Run 4.4 -> 4.5 -> 4.6 to prove the SAME precedence holds for mcp-authz's 403 insufficient_scope response, not just mcp-auth's 401 — mcp-authz independently reads gatewayUrl via shared metadata and builds its own WWW-Authenticate header. Run 4.7 to clean up.

item.name: 4.1 Deploy MCP Proxy (vhost set, mcp-auth, no gatewayUrl override in params)

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{precedenceProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: GatewayUrl Precedence Test
  version: v1.0
  context: {{precedenceProxyContext}}
  vhost: {{precedenceVhost}}
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: mcp-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers:
          - mock-jwks
    - name: mcp-authz
      version: v1
      params:
        tools:
          - name: add
            scopes:
              anyOf:
                - {{mcpAuthzRequiredScope}}
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: vhost is deliberately set (and must route real traffic, verified separately with `Host: {{precedenceVhost}}`) so 4.2/4.3 prove gatewayUrl wins over an ACTUALLY-ROUTING vhost, not just an unused config field. gatewayUrl/gatewayHost are deliberately NOT set in params here — they come entirely from config.toml's systemParameters, which is the whole point: this proves the live resolution pipeline, not a hand-built params map. mcp-authz is also attached (scope-gated on the "add" tool) so 4.6 can prove mcp-authz's own WWW-Authenticate generation also honors gatewayUrl precedence, not just mcp-auth's.

item.name: 4.2 Initialize - No Token via vhost (expect gatewayUrl in WWW-Authenticate, not vhost or gatewayHost)

request.description: The explicit Host header is what makes Envoy match this request to the {{precedenceVhost}}-scoped route at all — without it (plain routerBaseUrl with its default Host: localhost) this 404s, proving the vhost route is real and gatewayUrl genuinely overrides live routing, not just an unused config value.

exec: pm.test('WWW-Authenticate uses gatewayUrl verbatim, not vhost or gatewayHost', function () {

item.name: 4.3 Get Protected Resource Metadata via vhost (expect gatewayUrl in resource field)

exec: pm.test('resource is exactly gatewayUrl + context + /mcp', function () {
pm.test('authorization_servers is unaffected — still the mock-jwks issuer', function () {

item.name: 4.4 Get JWT Token (no scope) from Mock JWKS
4.5 Initialize via vhost WITH token (expect 200 — mcp-authz doesn't gate initialize)
4.6 tools/call add WITHOUT scope via vhost (expect 403, WWW-Authenticate uses gatewayUrl — proves mcp-authz's own header generation, not just mcp-auth's)

exec: pm.test('mcp-authz WWW-Authenticate uses gatewayUrl verbatim, not vhost or gatewayHost', function () {

item.name: 5 - MCP Authz Functional Test
item.description: End-to-end test for the `mcp-authz` policy, which runs after `mcp-auth` in the chain and authorizes individual MCP tools/resources/prompts/methods by required scope/claim. Uses the `scopes` (allOf/anyOf) form, not the deprecated `requiredScopes`. Requires the same default IT stack as folder 1.

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{mcpAuthzProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: MCP Authz Postman Test
  version: v1.0
  context: {{mcpAuthzContext}}
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: mcp-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers:
          - mock-jwks
    - name: mcp-authz
      version: v1
      params:
        tools:
          - name: "add"
            scopes:
              anyOf:
                - "{{mcpAuthzRequiredScope}}"
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: mcp-authz must come after mcp-auth in the policy chain — it reads the AuthContext mcp-auth already populated rather than authenticating on its own. Only the 'add' tool is gated; other tools/resources/prompts/methods are ungoverned (no rule matches them).

item.name: 5.2 Get JWT Token (no scope) from Mock JWKS
5.3 Initialize with unscoped token (expect 200 — mcp-authz doesn't gate initialize)

exec: pm.test('WWW-Authenticate names the missing scope', function () {

item.name: 5.5 Get JWT Token WITH required scope

exec: pm.test('Status code is 200 with the required scope', function () {

item.name: 6 - MCP Authz Policy Params Validation (additionalProperties)
item.description: mcp-authz's top-level `parameters.additionalProperties` was also switched from `false` to `true` (see gateway-controllers commit 7079679 on the mcp branch), same as mcp-auth in folder 2.3. This locks in that intentional behavior change for mcp-authz specifically.

item.name: 6.1 [Allowed] mcp-authz silently accepts unknown param (additionalProperties changed to true)

body.raw:
apiVersion: gateway.api-platform.wso2.com/v1
kind: Mcp
metadata:
  name: {{mcpAuthzAllowedProxyId}}
spec:
  displayName: MCP Authz AdditionalProperties Now Allowed Test
  version: v1.0
  context: /mcpauthzallowed
  specVersion: "2025-06-18"
  upstream:
    url: http://mcp-server-backend:3001/mcp
  policies:
    - name: mcp-auth
      version: v1
      params:
        issuers:
          - mock-jwks
    - name: mcp-authz
      version: v1
      params:
        tools:
          - name: "*"
            scopes:
              anyOf:
                - "mcp:tools:invoke"
        unknownExtraParam: "silently-accepted"
  tools: []
  resources: []
  prompts: []

request.description: mcp-authz requires at least one of tools/resources/prompts/methods to be present (anyOf), so a valid minimal rule set is included alongside the unrecognized top-level param.

exec: pm.test('Status code is 201 (accepted despite unknown param)', function () {
